title: Excellent and quasi-excellent commutative rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. It is *quasi-excellent* if it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], and J-2. Here J-2 means that for every finite type $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ for which $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. It is *excellent* if it is quasi-excellent and universally catenary. For a Noetherian $R$, universally catenary means that every finite type $R$-algebra $A$ is catenary: for any primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $A$, the lengths of all finite chains of primes between them have a common finite upper bound, and all saturated chains between them have the same length. A chain is saturated when no prime can be inserted strictly between consecutive members; its length is its number of strict inclusions.
